https://www.aol.co.uk/articles/tesco-giv.text: Taila Nichole Thompson Updated Tue, 28 July 2026 at 10:05 pm UTC 0 Tesco is giving away free groceries this week (Image: Getty) Holidaymakers returning to the UK this week may have received a free bag of groceries as part of a new giveaway from Tesco . The supermarket teamed up with easyJet holidays and London Southend Airport to hand out complimentary bags packed with everyday essentials to passengers arriving on selected flights. The giveaway comes after Tesco research found that one in four Brits say coming home to an empty fridge is one of the most frustrating parts of returning from holiday. The free bags were available in the airport's baggage reclaim hall on Tuesday, July 29, for passengers arriving on selected easyJet flights between 12pm and 5pm. Between 12pm and 5pm this week passengers can claim free bag (Image: Getty) Each bag includes a range of groceries, including tea bags, milk, bread, baked beans, cheddar cheese, strawberries, carrots, cucumber and custard creams, along with a bottle of aloe vera body lotion. Tesco's research found that a cup of tea tops the list of things holidaymakers crave when they return home, with 57% saying it's the first thing they want after a trip. Fresh milk was also high on the list, while more than a quarter said they would reach for a custard cream. The survey also found that nearly a third of people look forward to a traditional Sunday roast after returning from holiday, while 70% said they try to eat healthier once they're back home. Passengers travelling through London Southend Airport on eligible flights will be able to collect the complimentary bags from the baggage reclaim area while stocks last. As part of the campaign, Tesco and easyJet holidays are also giving away 10 £250 Tesco vouchers via Instagram, while one winner will receive an easyJet holidays getaway worth £1,500. https://www.laois-nationalist.ie/news/da.text: Sat, 19 Sep, 2026 - 18:44 Dad died after arm severed at work The 32-year-old from catastrophic injuries, when his left arm was severed from his body Donatas Jokubauskas       Seán McCárthaigh A YOUNG married father of one died from catastrophic injuries when his left arm was severed from his body, after getting trapped in a machine at a concrete plant, an inquest has heard. Donatas Jokubauskas (32), a native of Lithuania, was pronounced dead at the scene of the fatal incident at his workplace at Flanagan Concrete Products in Rathangan, Co Kildare on 31 May 2021. A sitting of Kildare Coroner’s Court heard that Mr Jokubuaskas became entrapped in the tail drum of a conveyor system at a batching plant within the facility. The inquest heard the deceased – who was known as ‘Donny’ to work colleagues – had been living in accommodation on the site of the concrete plant with his wife, Laura and one-year-old son, Arijus. Ms Jokubauskas told the inquest that they had married in July 2017, and her husband had moved to Ireland three months later after his uncle had found him a job before she joined him the following month. A director of Flanagan Concrete Products, Bernard Flanagan, gave evidence that he and Mr Jokubauskas had gone into the batching plant at around 10.30am as he was concerned about a spillage of aggregate on the equipment. The inquest heard that Mr Jokubauskas had recommended that a piece of rubber was needed for the machine. Mr Flanagan said a guard was in place on the machinery before he left to go find a measuring tape. As he was returning to the plant, Mr Flanagan said he heard a scream before discovering his employee was seriously injured and raising the alarm. Other work colleagues including the deceased’s uncle, Andrius Jokubauskas, gave evidence of trying to provide first aid to the injured worker and stop his bleeding before emergency crews arrived at the scene. Another staff member, Andrius Rimkus, said Mr Jokubauskas had lost a huge amount of blood and was not talking, while a driver, Niall Moore, described how he had placed the severed arm in a bag. Paramedic, Frank O’Connor, who arrived at the factory at 11.43am, said the victim was still alive but had suffered a traumatic amputation injury. While an air ambulance had also arrived at the scene, the inquest heard Mr Jokubauskas went into cardiac arrest at 11.49am and medical assistance was withdrawn 15 minutes later. An inspector with the Health and Safety Authority, Vincent Darcy, said an investigation had established that a protective guard had been removed from the batching plant to access the conveyor system. The inquest heard that while the equipment was being examined by Mr Jokubauskas, the machine was started at around 10.40am by a plant operator who was located in a separate office, trapping the victim between a tail drum and a conveyor belt. The HSA inspector said there were no direct witnesses to the fatal incident. Mr Darcy said a number of health and safety matters identified at the scene were addressed by the company’s management. In March 2026, Flanagan Concrete Products was fined a total of €80,000 at a sitting of Naas Circuit Criminal Court after the company pleaded guilty to two breaches of the Safety, Health and Welfare at Work Act 2005. They related to the failure to ensure a weight conveyor was not operated while a safety trip wire was inoperative and the failure to ensure that guards provided were not easily removed or rendered inoperative. Mr Darcy confirmed to counsel for Flanagan Concrete Products, Remy Farrell SC, that neither failure was a factor in Mr Jokubauskas’s death. Mr Farrell acknowledged that health and safety regulations made it dangerous for the guards to be removable without the use of tools. Kildare county coroner, Loretta Nolan, said a postmortem showed Mr Jokubauskas had died from hypovolemic shock from a severed left arm as a result of a workplace incident. Dr Nolan recorded a verdict of death by misadventure which she said was appropriate but not a sign of apportioning any blame. Offering her condolences to the deceased’s wife and work colleagues, the coroner remarked: “It was an awful tragedy for you. There are no other words to describe what happened.” More in this section Missing persons appeal stood down after the discovery of a body Schoolboy artist from Laois in Texaco winners’ show Two men arrested at scene of break-in in Graiguecullen Rathangan Donatas Jokubauskas Kildare Coroner’s Court  Large crowd enjoys Slieve Bloom walk READ NOW Latest Camross power past O’Moores to reach Intermediate final Portlaoise aim to finish the job as The Heath target long-awaited triumph History on the line as Sarsfields and Timahoe prepare for inaugural Junior ‘B’ final Large crowd enjoys Slieve Bloom walk Subscribe to the Laois Nationalist digital edition today from just €1.50 per week Laois Nationalist Newsletter Get Laois news delivered directly to your inbox. https://telex.hu/kulfold/2026/10/17/oros.text: Menü Kereső Reagált Zelenszkij az orosz szankciós csomag felfüggesztésére, szerinte a „szankciós áramszünet” újabb motivációt ad Putyinnak Külföld Madzin Emília Állítsd be a Telexet megbízható forrásnak! Beállítom Szankciós áramszünetként hivatkozott Volodimir Zelenszkij ukrán elnök az X-en Donald Trump döntésére, miszerint az amerikai elnök felfüggesztette az orosz gazdaságot célzó átfogó szankciós csomagot. „Az amerikai szankciós áramszünet, az agresszorra nehezedő nyomás enyhítése, Putyinnak nyújtott pénzügyi jutalmak – mindez csak arra ösztönzi őt, hogy folytassa a támadásokat”, írta. Donald Trump bejelentette, nemzeti érdekre hivatkozva Trump felfüggesztette az Oroszországot célzó új szankciós csomagot, aminek eredetileg az lett volna a célja, hogy fokozza a nyomást Oroszországra a 2022-ben megkezdett ukrajnai inváziója miatt. Ennek előzményeként Trump és Vlagyimir Putyin orosz elnök dízelmegállapodást kötöttek, amivel lényegében felrúgta az orosz energiahordozók exportjára vonatkozó amerikai szankciókat. Mindeközben pénteken és szombaton is folyamatosan támadták az oroszok Ukrajnát, összesen kilenc ukrán régiót értek orosz támadások, Ukrajna-szerte legalább nyolc ember meghalt és 60-an megsebesültek. Két bevásárlóközpontot is támadás ért, és az energiahálózat elleni csapások miatt több mint egymillió ember maradt órákra áram nélkül, írta a Reuters hírügynökség. Zelenszkij erről azt írta az X-en, hogy ebben a kritikus időszakban „Amerikában sajnos úgy döntöttek, hogy teljesen figyelmen kívül hagyják a Lindsey Graham-törvényt, aminek célja az volt, hogy valóban hatékony nyomást gyakoroljon Oroszországra a háború befejezése érdekében”. Az ukrán elnök szerint a törvény még mindig hatalmas segítséget jelenthet, de ahhoz minden támogató hangra szükségük van. Az ukrán energiaügyi minisztérium később azt közölte, az áramellátást több mint egymillió ember számára helyreállították, akik a pénteki orosz támadások következtében maradtak áram nélkül. A Lengyelországgal határos északnyugati Voliny régióban egy élelmiszer-feldolgozó üzem ellen indított dróncsapás során egy ember meghalt, nyolcan megsérültek, közölte Roman Romanyuk kormányzó. Elmondása szerint reggel 370 ezer ember maradt átmenetileg áram nélkül, bár közülük 100 ezernek később helyreállt az áramellátás. További támadások legalább két bevásárlóközpontot értek, az egyiket az északi Szumiban, ami a frontvonal közelében fekszik, a másikat pedig a szomszédos Rivne régióban. Időközben az orosz védelmi minisztérium szombaton közölte, hogy éjszaka nagyszabású támadást hajtott végre ukrán infrastrukturális célpontok ellen, köztük az ország legnagyobb acélgyárát, a Krivij Rih városában található üzemet. Az üzem tulajdonosa az acélipari óriásvállalat, az ArcelorMittal, ami szeptemberben több orosz ballisztikus rakétatámadás után felfüggesztette a létesítmény működését. A közlemény szerint az orosz erők eltaláltak egy villamosenergia-alállomást is Zsitomir városában, valamint egy másik acélgyárat Zaporizzsjában, a frontvonal közelében fekvő városban. A közlemény szerint egy Fekete-tengeri teherhajót is eltaláltak, és azt állították, hogy az katonai rakományt szállított Ukrajna odesszai kikötőjébe. https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-10-16/a.text: Explore the ABC Canberra man caught returning to Australia with alleged child abuse material denied bail H By Harry Frost Topic: Child Sexual Abuse Posted Fri 16 Oct 2026 at 4:50pm Fri 16 Oct 2026 at 4:50pm Fri 16 Oct 2026 at 4:50pm , updated Fri 16 Oct 2026 at 4:54pm Fri 16 Oct 2026 at 4:54pm Fri 16 Oct 2026 at 4:54pm Australian Border Force officers allegedly discovered child exploitation images on Nicholas Quinn's electronic devices when he re-entered the country. ( ABC News: Avani Dias ) In short: A man has been charged with possessing child abuse material after a search of his electronic devices when he returned to Australia from Europe. Police allege Nicholas Quinn, 42, has been maintaining a relationship with a 17-year-old girl in Ukraine. What's next? Mr Quinn was refused bail, with his case to return to court next month. abc.net.au/news/act-man-return-country-child-abuse-material-denied-bail/107276254 Link copied Share Share article A 42-year old Canberra man allegedly caught returning to Australia with child abuse material has been refused bail. Support services for those affected by child sexual abuse: Bravehearts : 1800 272 831 Lifeline (24-hour Crisis Line): 131 114 Victims of Crime Helpline : 1800 819 817 Full Stop (24-hour helpline for survivors of sexual assault and abuse): 1800 385 578 Australian Border Force officers selected Nicholas Tyson Quinn for examination after he landed in Sydney on a flight from Europe in May. It is alleged they found child exploitation images as well as inappropriate conversations on a messaging app, with further investigation uncovering multiple transfers of money to a teenager in Europe. ACT police raided Mr Quinn's home in Chisholm yesterday, where it is alleged they found a USB storage device containing child abuse material plugged into his computer. He faced the ACT Magistrates Court today, charged with two counts of possessing child abuse material. Nicholas Quinn was charged with two counts of possessing child abuse material. ( ABC News: Matt Roberts ) Applying for bail, Mr Quinn's lawyer told the court he could comply with conditions including living at home with his mother and surrendering his passports. But the prosecutor opposed his release, alleging Mr Quinn had been in a relationship with a 17-year-old girl in Ukraine, and his mother had previously travelled there with him and met with the teenager and her mother. The court heard Mr Quinn's employers allegedly told police about the travel to Ukraine, and that he had been trying to move his "girlfriend" to Australia. Concerns about persistent contact with young person, dual citizenship As an Australian and Latvian dual citizen, the prosecutor argued bail conditions could not prevent Mr Quinn from seeking a new Latvian passport in order to flee the country. Magistrate Alexandra Burt said the prosecution had not been able to confirm whether police believe the Ukrainian girl was depicted in the child abuse material. Despite being unable to confirm that detail, she refused bail due to the likelihood of Mr Quinn attempting to flee or endangering the safety of others. "Ultimately, there is a degree of speculation in those risks, I accept," Magistrate Burt said. "It is a case where the investigation is at a fairly preliminary stage. "I am concerned, partly because of the persistence of contact after the Australian Border Force intervention and of the connection with these two people — one of which is a young person — in Ukraine … and his dual citizenship." Mr Quinn was remanded in custody to return to court next month.
